question: A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician for gradual worsening of her vision. Her father died at 40 years of age. She is 181 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 69 kg (152 lb); BMI is 21 kg/m2. A standard vision test shows severe myopia. Genetic analysis shows an FBN1 gene mutation on chromosome 15. This patient is at greatest risk of mortality due to which of the following causes?

options.opa: Obstruction of the superior vena cava lumen
options.opb: Increased pressure in the pulmonary arteries
options.ope: Intimal tear of the aortic root

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "FBN1 gene mutation" -> "connective tissue disorder" -> "increased risk of aortic dilation" -> "possible aortic dissection" -> "intimal tear of the aortic root" -> 85%
CHAIN: "FBN1 gene mutation" -> "Marfan syndrome" -> "cardiovascular complications" -> "aortic root involvement" -> "risk of aortic rupture" -> "intimal tear of the aortic root" -> 90%
CHAIN: "FBN1 gene mutation" -> "weakened connective tissue" -> "aortic aneurysm formation" -> "risk of dissection" -> "intimal tear of the aortic root" -> 80%
CHAIN: "FBN1 gene mutation" -> "Marfan syndrome" -> "increased risk of cardiovascular events" -> "aortic complications" -> "intimal tear of the aortic root" -> 88%
analysis: The patient has a mutation in the FBN1 gene, which is associated with Marfan syndrome. Individuals with Marfan syndrome are at increased risk for cardiovascular complications, particularly involving the aorta. The most significant risk is the development of aortic dilation and dissection, which can lead to an intimal tear of the aortic root. Given the patient's severe myopia and family history of early mortality, it is likely that her father also had Marfan syndrome, which further supports the risk of aortic complications. Therefore, the greatest risk of mortality in this patient is due to an intimal tear of the aortic root.
